data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Hexagonal toroidal packing strictly requires periodic boundaries, whereas the unit square has hard boundaries which introduces severe edge constraints.","The unit square is a bounded polygon, not a continuous flat torus.","13 points do not perfectly tile into a hexagonal lattice without boundary defects, unlike 12 or 16 points."],"overturn_conditions":["If the hexagonal packing yields triangles smaller than 0.005 when cropped to the unit square boundaries.","If the lattice spacing required to maintain the minimum area pushes points outside the [0,1]x[0,1] bounds.","If a different lattice type (e.g., rectangular) provides a higher minimum area for 13 points."],"shared_structure":["Both involve distributing a fixed number of points to maximize the minimum area of any formed triangle.","Both aim to uniformly distribute points to avoid small triangular gaps.","Both are constrained by the density of points per unit area."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001"],"transfer_claims":["The optimal packing of 13 points in a flat torus translates to a near-optimal packing in the unit square, modulo boundary adjustments.","The minimum triangle area scales proportionally with the density of the points.","Maximizing the minimum distance between points generally maximizes the minimum triangle area."]},"claim":"A configuration based on a perturbed 4x4 grid with 3 omitted points, achieving a minimum triangle area of 0.005208. By systematically removing 3 points from a 16-point grid (e.g., removing three corners), we can slightly perturb the remaining 13 points outwards to expand the smallest triangles, securing a score above the 0.005 threshold.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the perturbation around the omitted points is too aggressive, it might shrink neighboring triangles below 0.005208.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the omitted points are not chosen symmetrically, the perturbation might cause an asymmetric collapse in minimum area.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the initial grid is too coarse, removing points cannot sufficiently increase the minimum area without violating boundaries.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A regular 4x4 grid in the unit square has a spacing of 1/3.
